title: Constant/limit ringed sequence projection and coherent reduction
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be sheaves of commutative rings with strict transition maps $q_{m,n}$ for $m\ge n\ge1$, and put $B=\varprojlim_n B_n$, with projections $\rho_n$. On $\mathcal V=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ put arrows $(V,k)\to(U,n)$ for $V\to U$ and $k\le n$, and the topology generated by coverings at a fixed index. Let $C_\bullet(U,n)=B_n(U)$, with horizontal restriction $q_{m,n}$, and let $\mathscr S(B_\bullet)$ be the category of strict semilinear module systems [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. There is a canonical exact equivalence $\operatorname{Mod}_{\mathcal V}(C_\bullet)\simeq\mathscr S(B_\bullet)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The constant-sequence functor and inverse limit form the inverse/direct-image adjunction of a geometric morphism $\pi:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], equipped with the ring map $\pi^{-1}B\to C_\bullet$ whose components are $\rho_n$.

On ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $L\pi^*$ is triangulated and for any flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] is represented by the single strict system $(P\otimes_B B_n)_n$ with transitions $1\otimes q_{m,n}$. These identifications are natural on derived morphisms. In particular its evaluation at $n$ is canonically $K\otimes_B^L B_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and its quotient maps compose before localization. Restriction at each level along $\rho_n$ defines an exact functor $U:\mathscr S(B_\bullet)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(B))$ [def-weil-inverse-system, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]; it retains the actual underlying additive transitions.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), constant/limit geometric morphism; Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), its K-flat pullback. The varying-ring module identification is the implicit prerequisite extracted here.

proof.text: Reindex $n\geq1$ by $n-1\in\mathbf N$. The product category and its fixed-index covering topology are those of [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. That statement supplies the ring sheaf $C_\bullet$, smallness relative to the module universe, and the explicit module equivalence, with vertical evaluation equal to level evaluation. In its functors a module sheaf restricts to its vertical slices; conversely a system restricts along $(V,k)\to(U,n)$ by its transition from $n$ to $k$ followed by restriction to $V$. These formulas preserve addition on morphisms. The category of strict systems has the componentwise abelian structure of [def-pur-system-level-left-extension-basic]; it is the system model of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], with the same actual transitions. Both sides are abelian, and [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions], clause (2), makes the additive equivalence exact. No condition that a transition be an epimorphism is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, first paragraph; varying-ring realization as in Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p.21

proof.text: A set-valued presheaf $F$ on $\mathcal V$ is equivalently a sequence of presheaves $F_n$ on $\mathcal C$: factor every arrow into a vertical arrow and an index arrow. Its sheaf equalizer for a generating covering at index $n$ is exactly that of $F_n$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Thus it is a sheaf precisely when every $F_n$ is, and its morphisms are exactly compatible level maps [def-weil-inverse-system]. The inverse construction sends $(U,n)$ to $F_n(U)$; the two constructions are inverse on sections and maps.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, first paragraph, the immediate sheaf/tower identification written out

proof.text: For a sheaf $H$ on $\mathcal C$, define $\Delta H$ to have value $H$ and identity index transitions. For a sheaf system $F$, let $LF(U)=\{(x_n):t_{m,n}(x_m)=x_n\}$, with componentwise restrictions. The small-limit assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] makes this a sheaf and its coordinate maps a limit cone. A map $H\to LF$ gives $\Delta H\to F$ by its coordinates; conversely a compatible family $h_n$ gives $x\mapsto(h_n(x))_n$. The two formulas are inverse and natural. Hence $\Delta\dashv L$. Finite limits on both sites are sectionwise by the same cited lemma; since $(\Delta H)(U,n)=H(U)$, $\Delta$ preserves them, including the terminal object. This is the geometric morphism $\pi$ of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with $\pi^{-1}=\Delta$ and $\pi_*=L$ on sets.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, constant/limit paragraph; sites.tex Tag 00W2, lemma-limit-sheaf

proof.text: The projections $\rho_n$ commute with vertical restrictions and satisfy $q_{m,n}\rho_m=\rho_n$, so they define the ring map $\Delta B\to C_\bullet$. By [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], module direct image has the underlying limit sheaf and the induced action $b\cdot(x_n)_n=(\rho_n(b)x_n)_n$. Consequently $\pi_*N=\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_{\rho_n}N_n$ as $B$-modules: [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] identifies the actions and [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] identifies the module limit and projections. For the constant ring $\Delta B$, a $\Delta B$-linear map $\Delta M\to N$ is a compatible family of $B$-linear maps, so the formulas in step 3 give the module adjunction $\Delta\dashv\lim$. All scalar actions here use the actual $\rho_n$, not any abstract identification of the coefficient sheaves.

source.place: Tag 03D6, definition-pushforward; Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, first paragraph

proof.text: For a $B$-module sheaf $M$ form $T(M)_n=M\otimes_B B_n$, with $t_{m,n}(x\otimes a)=x\otimes q_{m,n}(a)$. The tensor relations and the strict identities for $q$ give semilinearity, composition and identity. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction] at each $\rho_n$. A system map $T(M)\to N$ is thereby the same as maps $h_n:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{\rho_n}N_n$ with $t_{m,n}h_m=h_n$: the inverse formula is $x\otimes a\mapsto a h_n(x)$, and both compatibility conditions are equivalent by checking $x\otimes1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] these are exactly $B$-linear maps $M\to\pi_*N$. On the sequence site, the same ordinary scalar adjunction for $\Delta B\to C_\bullet$, combined with the module constant/limit adjunction of step 4, says that $C_\bullet\otimes_{\Delta B}\Delta M=\pi^*M$ has this same Hom correspondence. The two inverse correspondences therefore give the canonical identification $\pi^*M\cong T(M)$, natural in $M,N$. Its level formula and transitions are the displayed formulas, on sheafified pure tensors; it does not assert that sections of a sheaf tensor are a sectionwise tensor product.

source.place: Tag 03D7, lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules, applied also to identity-topos scalar extension; Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p.21, formula for pi-star

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] to the ringed morphism just constructed. Its size hypothesis holds since $\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ and $\mathcal C$ are small in the module universe (step 1). It gives the exact triangulated functor $L\pi^*$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories and a natural comparison $L\pi^*Q\to Q\pi^*$ invertible on K-flat complexes with flat terms. Such a resolution $p:P\to K$ exists by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The comparison $L\pi^*(K)\xrightarrow{L\pi^*(p)^{-1}}L\pi^*(P)\xrightarrow{\epsilon_P}\pi^*P$, followed by step 5 degreewise, represents it by the single strict complex $(P\otimes_B B_n)_n$. In particular the resolutions are chosen once over $B$, before any evaluation. The cited derived-pullback theorem sends quasi-isomorphisms between these representatives to quasi-isomorphisms of the entire sequence-site complex and supplies composition-compatible comparisons.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, statement and proof; Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution

proof.text: Evaluation is exact and is localized termwise by [def-pur-system-level-left-extension-basic] (and agrees with vertical restriction by [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]). Evaluating the representative of step 6 at $n$ gives $P\otimes_B B_n$, which computes $K\otimes_B^L B_n$ by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. On maps of K-flat representatives both comparisons send a chain map $a$ to $a\otimes1$. They commute with homotopies by applying tensor to the homotopy, and with inverses of quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Thus they agree on the localization, where arrows are composites of images of homotopy-category maps and such inverses. This proves naturality on derived morphisms, as well as independence of the chosen resolution; it is not merely an identification of object values.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change, localization construction and K-flat comparison; exact evaluation in Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p.21

proof.text: For $l\ge m\ge n$, both composites from $P\otimes_B B_l$ to $P\otimes_B B_n$ send a sheafified pure tensor $x\otimes a$ to $x\otimes q_{m,n}(q_{l,m}(a))=x\otimes q_{l,n}(a)$; equality on these generators is equality of sheaf tensor maps [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Equality indices give the identity map. The differentials and the tensor maps from any chain map commute with these transitions by their displayed formulas. Hence the maps already form a strict system of complexes before localization.

source.place: Tag 0940, section-derived-limits, actual inverse systems, with the tensor transition formula of Zheng Construction 4.1

proof.text: For a system $N$ leave its additive transition maps unchanged and restrict each component along $\rho_n$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. They are $B$-linear: $t_{m,n}(\rho_m(b)x)=q_{m,n}(\rho_m(b))t_{m,n}(x)=\rho_n(b)t_{m,n}(x)$. The same coordinate maps define the action on system morphisms and respect identities and composition. Restriction at each level preserves finite limits and finite colimits by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-coefficient-ordinary-adjunction]. Exactness of the source is componentwise by [def-pur-system-level-left-extension-basic], and exactness of the target tower category is componentwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Therefore this is the required exact functor $U$ retaining the actual underlying additive transitions.
